Allocation and teardown behaviour of new_inode, d_make_root, set_default_d_op and kill_anon_super.
Path handling of failfs_get_root, set_fs_pwd and path_put used during chdir to failfs root.
Permission, ownership and capability checks in inode_owner_or_capable and append only plus immutable predicates.
Implementations of fcntl_getlk, fcntl_setlk, fcntl_setlease, fcntl_getdeleg, fcntl_setdeleg, fcntl_dirnotify, pipe_fcntl and memfd_fcntl dispatched by do_fcntl.
Insertion and update semantics of fasync_insert_entry and lifecycle of fasync_struct beyond alloc and free.

findings.text: failfs_current_chdir is a non static helper that obtains the failfs root path, installs it as the current process working directory, releases the path reference, and reports success.

failfs denies access at every hook. Permission, lookup, getattr, statfs and weak revalidate each report operation not supported. Lookup is described as unreachable because permission already fails component walks, while weak revalidate covers jumps that land directly on the root without a permission check, preventing pinning by path only opens or handle encoding.
The directory inode operations table wires permission, lookup and getattr to the failfs denying helpers, so all directory metadata checks funnel to the same failure.
The dentry operations table wires weak revalidate and dynamic naming. The naming helper renders the root with a failfs label through the dynamic name facility.
The super operations table exposes only statfs, and the context operations table exposes only get tree, both pointing at the failfs denying or single instance helpers.
The file system type is registered under the name failfs with an init context hook and an anonymous super teardown hook. Its directory file operations table is empty and offers no handlers.

Superblock setup assigns large file size limit, page sized blocks with matching shift, failfs magic, the failfs super operations, no export or extended attribute hooks, unit time granularity and zero dentry flags. It allocates a root inode as a directory with link count two, number one, immutable flag and timestamp init, attaches the failfs inode and file operations, installs default dentry operations, and makes the root dentry, failing with out of memory if inode or root creation fails.

Single instance mount helper forwards the caller fill super routine and a single super test predicate to the virtual filesystem super acquisition path. The failfs get tree helper supplies its own fill super routine.
Context initialization points at the failfs context operations, marks the context global, adds a no user super flag, and adds no exec plus no device internal flags.
The settable file status mask is the union of append, nonblock, ndelay, direct and noatime.

Status flag update rejects clearing append on append only inodes open for write, rejects adding noatime without ownership or privilege, maps ndelay to nonblock when they differ, rejects direct on non FIFOs lacking direct capability, consults an optional driver check hook, and invokes the async hook only when the async bit changes before committing.
The final flag and io control flag commit is performed while holding the file spin lock, preserving bits outside the settable mask.

Owner allocation is a no op when the owner block already exists, otherwise allocates a zeroed block, initializes its read write lock, links the file, and discards the fresh block if a concurrent setter won the compare exchange.
Owner release drops the stored pid reference if an owner block exists and then frees the block.

Privileged owner update warns when the owner block is missing, otherwise takes the owner write lock with interrupts disabled and, when forced or no pid is stored, swaps in the new pid with reference handling and type, and when a pid is supplied records caller credentials plus a security hook call.

Numeric owner update defaults to thread group, treats negative values as process group with an explicit minimum integer guard against negation overflow, allocates the owner block, looks up the numeric pid under read copy update protection, reports missing pid as no such process, and applies the result with force.
Deletion clears the owner with a forced null update. Query returns zero when no owner exists or the target is dead, otherwise the numeric pid negated for process groups.

Extended owner exchange translates thread, process and group selectors between user and kernel pid type encodings, rejects unknown selectors, allocates the owner block on set, reports unknown pids as no such process, forces the update on set, and on get reports the stored type even when no pid or dead target yields zero pid, warning on impossible stored types.

One owner uid variant maps stored user and effective user ids into the caller user namespace, defaulting to zero without an owner block, and writes the pair to user memory with per word put status combined. The alternate build always reports invalid argument.

Owner reads hold the owner read lock with interrupts disabled and additionally hold read copy update protection while testing target liveness. Owner writes hold the owner write lock with interrupts disabled.
Valid write life hints are the six values not set, none, short, medium, long and extreme, with compile time assertions tying kernel and user encodings together.

Hint query copies the inode hint to user memory. Hint update rejects immutable inodes and callers lacking ownership or privilege, copies the value from user, validates membership, stores it to the inode, and also stores it to the mapping host inode when the mapping points elsewhere.

Duplicate descriptor query reports bad descriptor when the source slot is empty, otherwise reports whether the slot file pointer equals the supplied file, releasing the temporary reference before returning because only pointer identity matters.

Creation query reports the created mode bit as boolean. Signal number handling validates the number on set, lazily allocates the owner block on set, stores the number on set, and returns the stored number or zero on get when no owner exists.

The file control dispatcher handles creation query, duplicate with and without close on exec, duplicate query, close on exec get and set, status get and set, POSIX and open file description lock get and set with 32 bit arch restrictions, owner get with forced success plus set, extended owner get and set, owner uid query, signal get and set, lease get and set, directory notify, pipe size, seals, read write hint get and set, and delegation get and set, copying lock and delegation payloads across the user boundary and defaulting unknown commands to invalid argument.

Close on exec update and descriptor allocation serialize on the files lock. Allocation starts at the requested start or cached next value, locates the next clear slot, reports too many open files at the limit, expands the table and retries when beyond current capacity, advances the cached next value, marks the slot open with close on exec handling, and asserts the slot was empty.
Free descriptor search first probes the remainder of the starting word, then uses the full words bitmap to skip fully used words, returning the table size when no slot is free.

Descriptor duplication rejects starts at or beyond the no file resource limit as invalid, otherwise allocates from that start to the limit with requested flags, and on success holds a file reference and publishes the file in the new slot.

File installation rejects backing files with a one time warning, takes a fast path under scheduled read copy update protection with a read barrier paired against table expansion unless a resize is in progress, and otherwise falls back to a slow path under the files lock; both paths assert the target slot was empty before publishing.

Descriptor layer hazards include too many files at the resource limit, races with table expansion requiring the slow path, misuse with backing files, and slot collision checks treated as virtual filesystem bugs.

Lease query requests the lease flavor, and when a lock context with leases exists takes the file semaphore for read and the context lock, expires stale entries to a disposal list, scans for an entry tied to the querying file with matching flavor, maps pending unlock or downgrade flags to unlocked or read type, releases locks, then frees disposed entries, defaulting to unlocked.

Lease timeout walks the context list under the held context lock, demotes entries past downgrade time to read, and for entries past break time optionally consults a manager timeout hook to decide removal before demoting to unlocked, queueing changes to the disposal list.

Lease modification assigns the requested type, clears the matching pending state, wakes blocked waiters, and on transition to unlocked clears file ownership and signal state, detaches async notification with an error log if async state unexpectedly remains, and deletes the context entry onto the disposal list.
A lease is recovered from its core by container offset. Disposal drains the list by unlinking each core entry and freeing the enclosing lease through a dedicated slab cache.
Lease scans hold the file read write semaphore for read and the inode context spin lock together, and the timeout helper asserts the context lock is already held.

Async notification helper routes disable to removal and enable to addition. Removal scans the list under file and global async locks, detaches the entry matching the file under the entry irq write lock, clears the async file bit and frees via read copy update. Addition allocates from a dedicated cache and inserts, freeing the fresh entry and reporting no new entry when an update of an existing entry occurred.
Async removal nests the file spin lock outside the global async spin lock, with the per entry irq write lock innermost during detachment.

Owner and control hazards include warning on missing owner block during forced update, invalid signal rejection, minimum integer negation guard, no such process on unknown pid, fault on user copy failure, invalid type on unknown extended selector, and delegation of async bit changes and flag vetting to driver hooks whose negative errors abort the update.
